sections.heading: 1. What is Food Security
points: **Food security** = availability, accessibility and affordability of food to **all people at all times**.

sub: **Accessibility** — food within reach of every person.
**Affordability** — enough money to buy adequate, safe, nutritious food.

points: Food security is threatened by **calamities (drought, flood), war, and price rises**; the poorest are most at risk.

sections.heading: 2. Who are Food-Insecure
points: The **poor** — landless labourers, casual workers, SC/ST, and people hit by disasters.
A **famine** = widespread death due to starvation and disease (e.g. the **Bengal Famine of 1943**).
Some states/regions (rain-fed, disaster-prone) are more food-insecure; **seasonal** hunger also exists.

sections.heading: 3. India's Food Security System
points: The **Green Revolution** made India **self-sufficient** in foodgrains.
The government maintains a **buffer stock** of grain (wheat and rice) procured by the **Food Corporation of India (FCI)** at a **Minimum Support Price (MSP)**.
The **Public Distribution System (PDS)** distributes this grain through **ration shops (fair price shops)** at low prices; cards: **APL, BPL, Antyodaya (AAY)** for the poorest.
The **National Food Security Act (2013)** made food a **legal right** for about two-thirds of the population.

sections.heading: 4. Other Schemes and Cooperatives
points: **Government schemes:** Midday Meal, Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS), Antyodaya Anna Yojana.
**Cooperatives** (esp. in the south/west) run fair-price shops and help provide affordable food (e.g. **Amul** in dairy).
**Academy of Development Science (ADS)** promotes grain banks.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Food security = availability + accessibility + affordability of food for all, always.
Bengal Famine = 1943.
Buffer stock procured by FCI at Minimum Support Price (MSP); distributed via PDS/ration shops.
Cards: APL, BPL, Antyodaya (AAY = poorest).
National Food Security Act 2013 = legal right to food (~2/3 population).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: Food security has **three** dimensions: availability, accessibility, **affordability**.
**Buffer stock** is procured by the **FCI** at the **MSP**; distributed through the **PDS**.
**Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY)** targets the **poorest** families.
The **National Food Security Act** was passed in **2013**.
